title: Reserved backend paths return 200 for missing routes
reasoning: When the frontend catch-all is registered, unmatched backend-reserved paths such as /api/unknown are handled by serve_spa and return a plain dict. FastAPI serializes that as a 200 OK response, even though the route is explicitly intended to be Not found. This breaks normal API 404 semantics and can mislead clients, monitors, and reverse proxies.
reproduction: With the frontend build enabled, request GET /api/does-not-exist. The catch-all route matches after the API router misses and returns {"detail":"Not found"} with status 200.
recommendation: Raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found") or return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail":"Not found"}) for reserved backend paths.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current health tests cover existing API endpoints and the no-frontend root path. They do not run with the frontend build present and do not assert the status code for an unknown /api/* path after catch-all registration.
suggestedRegressionTest: With a frontend build fixture enabled, assert GET /api/not-a-route returns 404 and JSON {"detail":"Not found"}, while a client-side route like /library still returns index.html with 200.
minimumFixScope: Change the reserved-path branch in serve_spa to emit a 404 response.
